lead: Grand Rapids plumbing deals with lake-effect cold, old homes, lead service lines and basements. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Grand Rapids.
risk: lead service lines, frozen pipes and basement backups
risk_short: lead lines, frozen pipes and basements
why: Heritage Hill, Eastown and Creston have homes from the 1850s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines in many cases. The city is replacing lead lines over time.
Lake-effect snow and cold freeze pipes near exterior walls. Heavy rain and Grand River flooding, as in 2013, back water into basements.
utility: City of Grand Rapids Water System
water: Grand Rapids pipes its water from Lake Michigan and treats it at the Lake Michigan Filtration Plant. It is moderately hard.
tips: Check the city's lead service line lookup.
Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in Heritage Hill, Eastown, East Hills, Creston, the West Side, Garfield Park, Alger Heights and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Grand Rapids Development Center, and plumbers must be licensed by Michigan LARA.

faq.q: Is Grand Rapids replacing lead water lines?
faq.a: Yes. Michigan rules require utilities to replace lead service lines, and Grand Rapids has a citywide program. You can look up your address on the city's website.
